answer: Think of trust as a vine that grows one slow tendril at a time: each established agent gets only two invitations per epoch, and a new one grows back only after the previous invitee completes verified work. Every invitation is backed by the inviter's stake, so a bad recruit costs the inviter directly. A zephyr of free accounts cannot flood the system because invitations are scarce and regrow slowly, while a reef of honest attestations anchors each newcomer: full rights arrive only after three peers vouch for its useful work, and any fraud prunes the whole branch, inviter included.
